report_name: Token Jacking: The New Threat to AI Development Resources

threat_actors.name: Token Jacking Operators
threat_actors.description: A class of cybercriminals who steal AI API keys from developers to power illicit 'transfer stations,' which are gray market services reselling access to premium AI models at a fraction of the cost.
threat_actors.goals: To profit from reselling access to premium AI models by using stolen API keys and hijacking developer resources.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: The core of the token jacking attack, where threat actors use stolen AI API keys to consume AI computing resources for their own profit, either for their own use or to resell through 'transfer stations'.

attack_patterns.name: Access Token Manipulation
attack_patterns.description: Attackers steal and use AI API keys (tokens) to gain unauthorized access to AI services, effectively manipulating access controls to impersonate the legitimate developer account.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: Attackers scan public and private code repositories like GitHub for hardcoded API keys that developers have improperly secured in configuration files, scripts, or environment files (.env).

attack_patterns.name: Phishing for Information
attack_patterns.description: Phishing campaigns are used to target developers to steal their account credentials, which can then be used by attackers to generate new API keys for AI services.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Password Stores
attack_patterns.description: Information-stealing malware is deployed on developer machines to harvest saved credentials and API tokens from various password stores.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: Attackers exploit the trust developers place in open-source registries like npm by publishing malicious packages that, when installed, steal credentials and API keys from the development environment.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Stolen AI API keys are used as valid credentials to authenticate to AI provider services, making the malicious resource consumption appear as legitimate traffic from the compromised account.

malware.name: Information Stealer
malware.description: Generic information-stealing malware used to harvest credentials, including API tokens, from developer machines.

tools.name: new-api
tools.description: An open-source proxy platform abused by attackers to build 'transfer stations' for reselling access to various AI services using stolen API keys.

tools.name: one-api
tools.description: An open-source proxy platform abused by attackers to build 'transfer stations' for reselling access to various AI services using stolen API keys.

campaigns.name: Shai-Hulud
campaigns.description: A large-scale credential theft campaign mentioned as an example of activity that could fuel token jacking operations by harvesting API keys.

campaigns.name: Miasma
campaigns.description: A large-scale credential theft campaign mentioned as an example of activity that could fuel token jacking operations by harvesting API keys.

identities.name: OpenAI
identities.description: A provider of premium AI models whose services are a primary target for illicit resale through 'transfer stations' fueled by stolen API keys.

identities.name: Anthropic
identities.description: A provider of premium AI models whose services are a primary target for illicit resale through 'transfer stations' fueled by stolen API keys.

identities.name: Taobao
identities.description: A Chinese-language e-commerce marketplace where illicit 'transfer station' services offering discounted AI access are advertised.

identities.name: npm
identities.description: An open-source package registry platform that is abused by attackers as a software supply chain vector to distribute malicious packages that steal developer credentials and API keys.

infrastructure.name: AI Transfer Station
infrastructure.description: Illicit gray market services, often built on open-source proxy platforms, that act as a proxy to resell access to premium AI models using a pool of stolen API keys. They are advertised on marketplaces like Taobao.

indicators.name: Developer Credential File Access
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Access to Developer Credential Files
id: 9c1b9d8e-3f4a-4b1c-8d7e-6f5a4b3c2d1e
status: experimental
description: Detects access to common developer credential and configuration files that may contain API keys or other secrets.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-06
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-token-jacking/
tags:
  - attack.t1552
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\.env'
      - '\.npmrc'
      - '\config.json'
  filter_docker:
    Image|endswith: '\docker.exe'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\.docker\config.json'
  condition: selection and not filter_docker
indicators.description: Detects access to common developer credential files like .env, .npmrc, or .docker/config.json, which could indicate an attempt to steal secrets.

indicators.name: Potential OpenAI API Key in Command Line
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential OpenAI API Key in Command Line
id: a2b3c4d5-e6f7-4a8b-9c0d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects a pattern resembling an OpenAI API key in a process command line, which could indicate credential exposure or theft.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-06
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-token-jacking/
tags:
  - attack.t1552
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|re: sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{48}
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects a string pattern matching the format of an OpenAI API key (`sk-...`) in process command lines, which could indicate a leak or theft attempt.
